name: Crossed-Subcube Critical-Pendant Obstructions
statement: Let $X=\{a,b,p,q\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\mathbin{\dot\cup}V$ have size $d\ge4$, and choose $\alpha,\beta\in\{0,1\}$. Delete from $2^X$ the two crossed wings based at $a$ and $b$, together with the optional $p$- and $q$-half-wings specified by $\alpha$ and $\beta$. The remaining family $\mathcal K_d^{\bowtie,\alpha,\beta}$ is a learning space with complementary invalid roots $R=\{b,p\}\cup V$ and $\bar R=\{a,q\}\cup U$ whose contraction-repair sets cover $X$. Its pendant extension $\mathcal Y_{d+1}^{\alpha,\beta}$ is therefore a contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cube of order $2^d-(2+\alpha)2^{|U|}-(2+\beta)2^{|V|}+2$.
proof: The deleted wings are downward closed relative to their anchor coordinates, so no union of retained states enters a wing; a direct deletion argument gives accessibility. Translating at either displayed root identifies its rooted-union holes with the opposite wing except for the shared state. The neighbor test gives two explicit repair sets whose union is every coordinate, and the critical-pair pendant theorem gives contraction minimality. Inclusion-exclusion over the wings yields the order formula.
comments: When $U=V=\varnothing$, the three values of $\alpha+\beta$ supply the order-13, order-12, and order-11 pointed base types not represented by the chain-and-punctured-fiber family.
